As for the "work" comment, I'm going to add a sentiment I've expressed before. This is more for the lurkers than it is for the people who post in these threads.

What do is work. What we do has taken us many, many years of practice. What we do has required we dedicate a huge part of our lives to mastering our craft. We share the results of our work. We don't do this because we're fishing for compliments, we do this because it's in our nature to want to perform for you. We do this because we want to give you the chance to emote. We do this because we want you to enjoy it.

I can only give you my estimates:

It's a lot of work. Between this thread, the lesson thread, and the greatest guitarist thread - I devote about 10 hours to it. That's a chunk of time and then I try to practice for 4 hours most every single day. Add to that four hours of in-person rehearsals with the band and we're looking at about 42 hours spent every single week of music-related activity.

And, for the 4 hours of daily practice, that's not counting the time spent noodling and just playing around. That's 4 hours of dedicated practice. I'll spend 2 hours just playing scales, another 30 minutes fingering chord progressions, another 30 minutes practicing a skill for the day (such as a particular attack), and an hour actually learning new material.

Some days, I may only practice for two hours - but I make up most of those by playing around more or by adding hours to another practice session. Some days, I have a guitar in my hand for 6 hours.

The difference is that I'm retired. I can do this. Well, I'm sort of retired. I kind of suck at being retired.

The point I'm trying to make is that I have that free time - and many goats don't. So, imagine the percentage of their "free" time these other goats dedicate to bringing you new music every week.

Really, imagine those hours.

It's work. It's not just work, it's tedious work. It's exacting (for varied levels of such) work. It's long periods of time just to master our craft, and we never truly master it. I'm going on 50 years of playing and there's still a ton of things I don't know.

By this giant wall of text, I'm trying to tell you that we do this not just for each other - but for you. If you lurk, don't be bashful - hop right in and thank some of them for having the courage to share and the dedication to make quality music. Trust me, every single person in these threads would love to hear that you enjoyed their work, that their work meant something to you, that their work was a source of inspiration, happiness, or a reason to think that this moment is the best day ever.

And, if you play and don't feel confident, I can tell you that each and every one of us sucked at one point. We don't care if you're a professional. We just care that you're playing.
